idea-plugin.name: ML Experiment Cockpit
idea-plugin.description:
MLflow experiment tracking, Weights & Biases (wandb) sweeps, Optuna studies, the Model Registry — runs and metrics in PyCharm, IntelliJ, WebStorm, GoLand or CLion.

  • Experiments — your MLflow experiments and runs in a tree, with parameters, metric values and the full history of any metric as a curve.
  • Optuna — studies and trials from your Optuna Dashboard: summary, the five best trials and the most-chosen hyperparameter.
  • Models — the MLflow Model Registry: registered models, their versions, stage, status and run id.
  • Sweeps — W&B hyperparameter sweeps grouped by state, with the best run and its top summary metrics.

All four tabs live in one ML Experiment Cockpit tool window, in PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, GoLand and CLion — any IntelliJ-platform IDE from build 243 to 263. This plugin is read-only: it reads your servers and never writes to them.

You see exactly what your server answers, within its own query limits: up to 500 experiments, 100 runs per experiment, 500 registered models, 500 model versions and 5 000 metric points per run; W&B sweeps are read without pagination (the first 50 sweeps).

It is a read-only MLOps view: experiment tracking, hyperparameter sweeps and registered models, read from the servers you configure. Open it from View | Tool Windows | ML Experiment Cockpit and set your servers in Settings | Tools | ML Experiment Cockpit. Every request goes to the servers you configure — no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.21 — New description, easier to find.

  • The plugin description on the Marketplace has been rewritten: it now names the four tabs (Experiments, Optuna, Models, Sweeps) and the servers they read, so the plugin shows up in searches that use the words buyers actually type.
  • No functional change: the plugin reads the same servers and shows the same data as in 0.0.20.

0.0.20 — Four display and read defects fixed.

  • Optuna and Models trees now show the readable label of each row (study name, model name, version) instead of the raw Kotlin dump (StudyNode(summary=…)).
  • The Optuna bar chart now picks the hyperparameter that takes the most distinct values, as documented; the numeric tie-breaker is only used when two parameters have the same number of values.
  • A mistyped Optuna URI (for example localhost:8080 without http://) is now reported as Failed to load studies instead of Unexpected error.
  • Optuna trials whose value is inf or -inf (sent as a string by the dashboard) are now read as Infinity and -Infinity; they used to show as “—” and to be left out of the ranking.

0.0.19 — Malformed numbers are reported as invalid JSON.

  • Numbers are now read with the exact JSON grammar (RFC 8259). A response holding a malformed number (for example 1., 1e or 01) is rejected as invalid JSON: the plugin now says that the server did not answer JSON, instead of failing with an opaque conversion error such as For input string: "1.".

0.0.18 — Run tooltips now show.

  • The tooltip of a run in the Experiments tree is now displayed when you hover it: Swing only shows a renderer's tooltip for a component registered with the ToolTipManager, so the run details were silently never shown. This fix was not part of the 0.0.17 build.

0.0.17 — Compatible with the 2026.3 IDE release, and clearer W&B errors.

  • The plugin now declares compatibility up to IDE build 263.*, so it keeps installing on PyCharm 2026.3 instead of becoming obsolete when that release becomes stable.
  • W&B tab: a GraphQL error now shows the server's own message (e.g. "Cannot query field …") instead of a bare "GraphQL error", and an unknown project is reported as "project not found" instead of an empty list.
  • The MLflow and Optuna tabs are unchanged.
